comprehensiveness.criterion: Coverage of major ethical frameworks relevant to autonomous weapon systems
Coverage of the full range of core ethical arguments and counterarguments about AWS
Inclusion of relevant empirical and operational evidence informing the debate
Coverage of legal and accountability frameworks tied to AWS regulation
Breadth of national approaches and comparative state positions
Coverage of international bodies, multilateral processes, and civil-society or expert initiatives
Attention to definitional, technical, and scope-setting debates
Inclusion of historical context, recent developments, and unresolved governance questions

insight.criterion: Critical evaluation of major arguments and counterarguments
Ability to connect ethical reasoning with regulatory and geopolitical positions
Conceptual precision and analytical handling of contested definitions
Synthesis of tensions, dilemmas, and unresolved questions

instruction_following.criterion: Directly answers the full research question
Covers both required subject domains without drifting beyond scope
Follows the mandated report structure and markdown-oriented organization
Includes an explicit Sources section at the end listing consulted references and URLs
Provides the specifically requested critical-analysis components

readability.criterion: Clarity and accessibility of language: The article uses precise, straightforward wording, defines technical/legal/ethical terms (e.g., AWS, meaningful human control, IHL) when first introduced, and avoids unnecessary jargon or unexplained acronyms.

Logical organization and flow: The report is structured with clear sections and subsections, smooth transitions, and an argument sequence that helps readers move from ethical frameworks to national positions and regulatory debates without confusion.
Sentence and paragraph readability: Sentences are concise and varied in length, paragraphs are focused on one main idea, and dense material is broken into digestible units that reduce reader fatigue.

Effective use of formatting and signposting: Markdown headings, bullet points, tables, emphasis, and topic sentences are used appropriately to highlight comparisons, key claims, and regulatory distinctions across countries and institutions.

Use of illustrative summaries and synthesis aids: Complex ethical arguments and governance positions are clarified through brief summaries, comparative tables, and synthesis statements that help non-specialist readers understand the main takeaways.
